correctness.rationale: The exact arithmetic script was executed successfully from its actual standalone path. It rederives p′±q′ rational factors from the original coefficient tails and verifies both identities. Cayley-transformed P4 satisfies strict quartic Hurwitz tests, ensuring the ratio is analytic throughout the closed unit disk. P6(-r) is strictly increasing and has a root in the exact rational bracket. Each of the six Bernstein coefficients of the boundary divided difference has a rigorously positive rational lower bound on the entire root bracket; hence Re[(p′+q′)/(p′-q′)] is nonnegative on the critical circle and strictly positive inside by the minimum principle, implying the exact Jacobian sign and unique boundary contact. Lewy’s theorem proves sharpness for local univalence. No unproved global-injectivity or external classification is asserted.

value.rationale: The canonical first bounded convex ellipse counterexample to Dorff’s convolution problem raises the natural and previously unanswered two-dimensional question of the largest centered disk before its self-convolution loses local univalence. A real-diameter fold location does not answer that question because off-axis folds could occur earlier. The new exact circle-wise certificate proves that no such folds occur and provides the sharp, reproducible first-contact modulus, a structural localization not an arbitrary slice or small numeric gain.
